result.rationale: Verified in the diff: refreshOAuthTokens in the sync-enabled branch returns the raw fetch Response (no JSON parsing) to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Google CalendarService then does `const token = res?.data` and `googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` — res.data is undefined on a fetch Response, so token.access_token throws a TypeError inside the existing try block, whose catch path then re-attempts handling/fails silently, defeating the refresh. This is a concrete correctness defect introduced by this diff.

record.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:92 — With credential sync enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, so `res.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws TypeError that is silently swallowed.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code assumes an axios-style response (`const token = res?.data;`). But `refreshOAuthTokens()` explicitly returns the raw `fetch()` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), and a `Response` does not have a `.data` property. In that credential-sync branch, `token` becomes `undefined`, so `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date` will throw at runtime.
